title: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
eligibility: All landholding farmer families across India (subject to specific exclusion criteria)
benefits: Direct income support of ₹6,000 per year transferred in 3 equal installments of ₹2,000 directly into bank accounts.
application_process: Apply via PM-KISAN web portal (pmkisan.gov.in) or nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with Aadhaar and land records.
content: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector Scheme providing financial assistance to landholding farmers for procuring agricultural inputs like seeds, fertilizers, and equipment.
source: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Govt. of India

title: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana)
eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas (loanee & non-loanee farmers)
benefits: Low premium rate paid by farmers: 1.5% for Rabi crops, 2.0% for Kharif crops, and 5.0% for Commercial/Horticultural crops. Balance premium subsidized by Govt.
application_process: Enroll through banks, insurance intermediaries, or PMFBY portal (pmfby.gov.in) before cut-off date.
content: PMFBY provides comprehensive crop insurance cover against yield loss due to non-preventable natural risks (drought, flood, cyclone, pests, localized hazards).

title: KCC (Kisan Credit Card Scheme)
eligibility: Individual/joint farmers, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, and self-help groups
benefits: Short-term credit for crop cultivation at concessional interest rate of 4% per annum (with 3% prompt repayment incentive). Limit up to ₹3 Lakh without collateral.
application_process: Apply at any commercial bank, regional rural bank (RRB), or cooperative bank branch.
content: KCC ensures adequate and timely credit support from the formal banking system to meet cultivation expenses, post-harvest needs, and working capital requirements.

title: Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme
benefits: Free soil testing report showing N, P, K, micro-nutrients, pH, and electrical conductivity, along with customized crop-wise fertilizer recommendations.
application_process: Contact District Agriculture Officer or local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK).
content: Soil Health Card promotes balanced fertilizer application, reduces unnecessary input costs, and improves long-term soil health.
